analysis.evidence: וַתְּהִי links the subject רֵאשִׁית מַמְלַכְתּוֹ (“the beginning of his kingdom”) to the four cities that constituted that beginning. The feminine singular verb agrees with the head noun רֵאשִׁית.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ is prefixed to a Qal wayyiqtol, third-person feminine singular, agreeing with רֵאשִׁית.
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: רֵאשִׁית מַמְלַכְתּוֹ means “the beginning of his kingdom.” The four cities that follow identify where his kingdom began.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the construct state, followed by מַמְלַכְתּוֹ (“his kingdom”).

analysis.evidence: The verse names Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh in the land of Shinar as the beginning of his kingdom. The list of cities identifies the kingdom as the territory he ruled.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the construct state with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix.
